title: Five-study contextual-search comparison
status: Archived research evaluation; not output from the offline demo or a new API run of this release.

design.eligibility: Two blinded coders assessed pooled pairs; both had to admit a pair.
design.coverage: One blinded coder per study assigned a common attribute vocabulary to eligible pairs pooled across both methods. Method labels and scores were hidden.
design.budget: Equal final context slots; generation and review calls were not matched.

metricDefinitions.yield: The number of eligible pairs whose changed-minus-reference rating differences have the same nonzero sign and absolute size at least 10 in both assessments, divided by all allocated slots.
metricDefinitions.magnitude: For each eligible complete pair, the smaller absolute difference across the two assessments when their signs agree; zero otherwise. Averaged over eligible complete pairs.
metricDefinitions.attributeCoverage: Number of distinct primary observable variables changed among eligible pairs, using one pooled coding vocabulary per study. Synonyms, reversed directions and different levels of the same variable are merged.
metricDefinitions.conceptCoverage: Number of distinct primary conceptual categories assigned to those variables. Seven project categories are available; clearly defined additional categories are retained.
metricDefinitions.aggregate: Yield pools all 50 allocated slots. Magnitude pools eligible complete pairs. Coverage averages the five study-specific counts; it is not a global unique count or a percentage.

studies.citation: Beckman, C. M., Haunschild, P. R., and Phillips, D. J. (2004). Friends or Strangers? Firm-Specific Uncertainty, Market Uncertainty, and Network Partner Selection. Organization Science, 15(3), 259-275. doi:10.1287/orsc.1040.0065.
studies.x: Market uncertainty: prior-year mean monthly stock-price coefficient of variation of sampled industry peers, excluding focal firm
studies.y: Annual count of additional alliances with existing alliance partners

studies.citation: Mitsuhashi, H., and Greve, H. R. (2009). A Matching Theory of Alliance Formation and Organizational Success: Complementarity and Compatibility. Academy of Management Journal, 52(5), 975-995.
studies.x: Market complementarity between potential liner-shipping alliance partners

studies.citation: Chung, S. (A.), Singh, H., and Lee, K. (2000). Complementarity, Status Similarity and Social Capital as Drivers of Alliance Formation. Strategic Management Journal, 21(1), 1-22.
studies.x: Status similarity: lower bank status divided by higher bank status
studies.y: Lead bank selects potential bank for stock-offering syndicate

studies.citation: Ahuja, G., Polidoro, F., Jr., and Mitchell, W. (2009). Structural Homophily or Social Asymmetry? The Formation of Alliances by Poorly Embedded Firms. Strategic Management Journal, 30(9), 941-958. doi:10.1002/smj.774.
studies.x: Potential partner network centrality conditional on focal firm having below-mean centrality

studies.citation: Lavie, D., and Rosenkopf, L. (2006). Balancing Exploration and Exploitation in Alliance Formation. Academy of Management Journal, 49(4), 797-818.
studies.x: Accumulated structure-exploration experience through preceding year: historical average indicator that alliance partner had no prior joint alliance
studies.y: Current-year structure exploration: average new-partner indicator over alliances formed that year

source.note: Compact numeric export from the frozen research archive. Study titles and field names are expanded for readability; numerical values are unchanged.
